cohort: The study included 2,964 women who attempted vaginal birth at a single center in Japan from 2012 to 2021, categorized into TOLAC (n=187) and non-TOLAC (n=2,777) groups.
finding: After adjusting for confounding factors and potential biases, cesarean scars had a limited, non-significant impact on labor duration in TOLAC participants compared to those without a prior C-section.
mod_finding: The study found that a prior cesarean section, when attempting TOLAC, did not significantly affect the duration of current labor after adjusting for confounding factors.
